title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a proposed law that prohibits the use of artificial intelligence for diagnosing and treating patients without a licensed medical professional overseeing or approving the care. It aims to safeguard patient safety, uphold professional standards, and ensure that only qualified doctors are responsible for clinical decision‑making.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 seeks to curb excessive pricing of AI services and protect workers from wage manipulation driven by automated systems. It proposes regulatory measures to ensure fair costs and safeguard labor market fairness.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to boost national competitiveness by expanding AI education at all levels, from K‑12 to higher‑education and vocational training, and by creating public and private partnerships to provide up‑skilling and reskilling opportunities for workers. It also establishes grant programs, research incentives, and certification pathways that help employers and employees adapt to the growing AI job market.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate has passed a resolution emphasizing that religious freedom and the use of authoritative texts must guide the development of AI systems. It also calls for greater transparency in these systems so that their decisions and underlying logic can be openly understood and examined.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, via the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to launch a pilot program that uses AI to protect critical infrastructure from cyber attacks. The program will test AI tools, collect data, and help shape future national cybersecurity strategies.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy requires the Director of National Intelligence to report to Congress how artificial intelligence systems are used under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The report must explain how AI helps acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information collected through that legal framework.

title: To require the Secretary of Homeland Security to carry out prize competitions to advance the science of interpretability and to develop adversarial robustness with respect to artificial intelligence products, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy orders the Secretary of Homeland Security to hold prize competitions that focus on making artificial‑intelligence systems easier to understand (interpretability) and harder to trick with malicious inputs (adversarial robustness). The aim is to spur research and development in these areas to improve national security and safety.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is designed to safeguard shoppers from misleading or deceptive AI practices. It sets out rules and oversight to ensure AI tools provide honest information and clear disclosures.

title: A bill to establish the Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes establishing a Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations to oversee and investigate incidents involving cybersecurity and AI technologies. It also includes additional measures and provisions to support and regulate these areas.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: This bill proposes creating a new fund called the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund, which would provide financial support for AI research, development, and innovation. It also includes additional provisions that the bill describes as “other purposes” without detailing those specific measures.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act is a proposed law designed to create rules for the creation, testing, and use of AI models, so they are safe and reliable. It focuses on making AI systems more transparent, accountable, and protected from harmful or unfair behavior.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: This act aims to shield families from the rising energy costs associated with AI data centers, which can drive up household electricity bills. By regulating or providing subsidies for the energy usage of these facilities, the policy seeks to prevent families from bearing higher utility expenses resulting from the growth of AI infrastructure.

title: Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act establishes a new federal department focused on researching, developing, and regulating advanced technology and AI. The act outlines the department’s mandate, governance structure, funding, and partnerships with industry and academia to promote innovation while ensuring ethical and responsible AI deployment.

title: A bill to establish the Department of Artificial Intelligence and to provide for the regulation of advanced artificial intelligence systems, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill proposes creating a new federal Department of Artificial Intelligence to oversee and regulate advanced AI systems. It also sets out rules, standards, and policies to ensure AI development is safe, transparent, and aligned with societal values.

title: A bill to require disclosure of certain information relating to artificial intelligence systems, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill requires developers of artificial intelligence systems to disclose detailed information about how the AI works, its training data, and potential risks. It also includes additional provisions aimed at improving transparency, accountability, and safety in AI deployment.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 aims to ensure that AI technologies used in veteran services are developed and deployed responsibly, prioritizing safety, transparency, and accountability. The law establishes guidelines and oversight mechanisms to protect veterans from bias, discrimination, and privacy violations while leveraging AI to improve healthcare, benefits, and support programs.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is proposed legislation aimed at regulating or curbing the development of artificial intelligence systems that could act unpredictably or pose significant risks to society. It seeks to establish safeguards, oversight, and accountability measures to ensure AI technology remains safe, ethical, and aligned with human values.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act seeks to set rules and oversight for using artificial intelligence in processing Veterans Affairs claims. It aims to make AI systems transparent, fair, and accountable so veterans’ rights are protected.

title: Covered AI Prohibition Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Covered AI Prohibition Act is a proposed law that bans the use of artificial intelligence in certain regulated areas. It aims to protect consumers and public safety by limiting AI deployment in specific industries and applications.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act mandates that defense contractors rigorously test and document the performance of AI systems before deployment to ensure safety and effectiveness. It also establishes a mandatory reporting framework for ongoing monitoring, incident reporting, and compliance audits to keep government authorities informed about AI system reliability and risks.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to disclose when and how artificial‑intelligence systems are used in veteran care, including the logic behind automated decisions and any associated risks. It also creates reporting obligations, oversight mechanisms, and safeguards to ensure veterans and regulators can understand and review these AI applications.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act aims to establish comprehensive safety standards for the development, testing, and deployment of advanced AI systems. It seeks to ensure that these technologies are secure, resilient, and aligned with national interests by requiring rigorous risk assessments, oversight mechanisms, and collaboration between industry and government.

title: Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act prohibits the use of artificial‑intelligence systems to automatically deny or reduce Medicare benefits, ensuring that coverage decisions remain under human or regulated oversight. The legislation aims to protect patients from algorithmic errors and maintain fairness in Medicare access.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on the construction and expansion of new AI data centers to address environmental, social, and regulatory concerns. It aims to give lawmakers and communities time to evaluate impacts, develop guidelines, and ensure responsible growth of AI infrastructure.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 seeks to protect AI model creators from unauthorized use or distribution by establishing penalties and legal recourse for model theft. It creates enforcement mechanisms—including civil and criminal liability—to ensure that AI technology is securely licensed and safeguarded against piracy.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 establishes a framework for studying how artificial intelligence is used in judicial settings and sets up an independent oversight body to monitor its impact. The law requires transparency, data protection, and continuous evaluation of AI tools to ensure fairness and accountability in court proceedings.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 is a law that sets out how the U.S. Small Business Administration and small businesses can use artificial intelligence safely and responsibly. It establishes clear guidelines, promotes transparency, and provides resources to help small firms adopt and manage AI technologies.

title: American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act aims to position the United States as a global leader in AI technology while ensuring consistent, nationwide standards for its development and deployment. The law likely sets up federal guidelines and oversight to promote innovation, safety, and ethical use of AI across all sectors.
